"Admissions," a play by Joshua Harmon now at Citadel Theatre, should have its audiences talking about who, how and why a graduating high schooler is readily admitted to the college of choice.

cn.t: Harmon's sharp dramedy about college admissions and white liberalism earns strong praise for its brilliant, piercing examination of deeply held beliefs under pressure, though it refuses easy answers to its provocative questions about race and privilege.
